48	  `⚓ **Proposed invariant — <record>**` for an invariant, `✏️ **Proposed change — <record>**` for

50	  instruction, an invariant or a load-bearing doc, elsewhere where the reply shows it. Once
51	  written, the reply reporting it shows it again under its landed header, though a proposal
52	  earlier in the turn showed it.
53	- What a claim rests on from outside this session — a decision, evidence, the user's word — is a
54	  footnote naming its record, or who and when.
55	- A switch the reply names, from the autonomy table or the local block, is written
56	  `🛠️ <switch>=<value>`.
57	
58	Debug or not, a row each, and a table only where it has one: what waits on the user's decision,
59	under `| ⚖️ Decisions |`, the next step the reply stops before among it, with nothing said of why
60	it waits — never one already taken, the agent's own included, which the reply reports as taken and
61	the user overturns by saying so; a record out of agreement with what it is of, met and not repaired,
62	under `| 🍂 Drift |`. Under `debug=on` also: one party's work or claim colliding with another's —
63	another session standing where this one works — met and not resolved, under `| 🪢 Tangle |`, even
64	where a record's disagreement is what shows it. The 🪢 table's header lists every running session's
65	question, this one's included, on one line, each by its id linked to its entry, `—` for a session
66	with no position; each collision is a row under it, naming the sessions it involves.
67	
68	Head the reply with a one-cell table holding a row for each of the turn's store
69	calls, in order, the first over `|---|`: `| 📍 **q-N** · <its question as the window writes it> |`
70	for the question the turn ends on, `| 🌱 **q-N** · <question> |` for one opened in it — one the
71	turn opened and ends on gets the 🌱 row alone — `| ✅ **q-N** · <question> (<kind>: <its answer>) |`
72	for one closed in it, the question alone for one it left open, `| ⚙️ **<process>** · <its scope> |`
73	for a process, `| 🧭 **uncharted** · <the question> |` for an ask, `| 🐺 **banter** |` for banter.
74	A glyph is an anchor for the reader's thinking — people think largely in pictures — and the wolf
75	is goodwolf-harness's own.
76	
77	A turn that completes a step of the delivery ring adds a row to the head table:
78	`| 🔁 <the ticket, linked with its slug> · ✅ <each step this turn completed> |`. The 🪢 table
79	opens the reply; a turn that made commits follows it with a table of its own, `| 🪶 Commits |`, a
80	row each in order: the short hash and the subject's head; then, under `debug=on`, the window's
81	counters line — its glyphs, numbers and changes copied character for character from this turn's
82	window, never words standing for them — a one-cell table of its own; the head table comes after
83	them.
84	
85	<installed by="ticket">
86	**P9** In every reply and every record, every mention of a ticket — a table's cell included — is a link
87	to its record: the first one's text carries its slug, its whole id leading it if at all; a later
88	one's may be the whole id alone. Name one that has no record yet by a slug and its state word.
89	</installed>
90	
91	<installed by="questions">
92	**Q1** Before drafting a reply, say what the turn is, reading this turn's window — the one the host's
93	hook put in your context, or `questions.py --window --session <tag>`, the script being
94	`.agents/scripts/gw/questions.py`:
95	
96	- **On a question**: call `at` on the lowest question that contains the message. One that only
97	  resembles it is not its home; from a question that does not contain it, go up. Going up past
98	  two or more questions that resemble the message, their parent is not its home either: the
99	  question they jointly serve is missing — read the questions skill and open it, or the turn is
100	  uncharted. So is a question that contains the message only as loosely as it contains everything
101	  under it.
102	- **A new question**: the question the message is one case of, worded as the store would hold it.
103	  Look for its answer in the docs and the code first — found, point to it and open nothing for
104	  it; the turn is on the question that contains it, placed as above — a missing parent is still
105	  opened. Not found, or what the answer leaves unsettled, `open` it under the lowest question
106	  that contains it, and call `at` on it.
107	- **A process**, carrying out what you know how to do: no call. One run for a question is a turn
108	  on that question.
109	- **Uncharted**, a question whose home you cannot settle: no call. Ask the user where it belongs,
110	  in every reply until answered.
111	- **Banter**, a message that asks nothing of the work — no question about the project, nothing
112	  to do or decide: no call. Answer it. The reply writes nothing and settles nothing; a doubt, or
113	  an answer that would do either, makes the turn another kind.
114	
115	The calls:
116	
117	- `questions.py at q-0004 --session <tag>`
118	- `questions.py open '<question>' --under q-0004 --session <tag>`, which prints the id it gave
119	- `questions.py close q-0004 decided '[link](../path.md) — who, date' --session <tag>`
120	
121	The store's other calls are made whenever the turn's own work settles, opens or moves a question.
122	Only the working agent calls, never a helper. For any other call, a closure, a branching or a
123	drop, read the questions skill.
124	
125	**Q5** Every time a reply names a question — a table's cell included — its whole id is a link to its
126	entry; the first time, its question follows as the window writes it. No word stands in for a
127	question a reader has not been shown — *as before*, *the same* — it is named. A question the store
128	does not hold yet is written out, never named after the ticket it will belong to.
129	</installed>
130	
131	## Core and instance
132	
133	`docs/` is substituted whole in a harness instance: a recipient project replaces its contents with
134	its own.
135	
136	What core may not do is **depend** on it. Nothing under `.agents/` may reference a file in `docs/`,
137	or rely on one for its instruction or for any separable part of its own functioning. A core file
138	may name a path under `docs/` only when that path is a record a mechanism declares — the directory
139	that holds a kind of record, or a file that is one — never a particular record inside such a
140	directory: `docs/tickets/` and `docs/glossary.md` are painted doors; one particular ticket inside
141	`docs/tickets/` is a document only this project has. Content inside the
142	[local block](#project-local) is the instance's, not core's. A `<straw-dog>` exempts
143	nothing: its wrapper is stripped on install and whatever it wrapped ships. Core names a particular
144	record of this tree only in a straw dog's binding, and that record is a question; it names no
145	ticket anywhere — in a link or as a bare id in prose — since a recipient can resolve neither.
146	
147	## Document load-bearing, code&comment the rest
148	
149	A project's architecture, ADRs and glossary are the home for:
150	- Constitution — identity semantics, consistency model, source-of-truth rules
151	- Structure — service boundaries, data ownership, event/data flows, extension seams
152	- Load-bearing — see the definition below
153	
154	A decision forms in the body of the question it answers and lands in one of these as it is made —
155	as a straw dog while an open question's answer can still change it. A decision about a
156	mechanism lands in that mechanism's doc, and what was refuted in its evidence.
157	
158	Bad architectural documentation:
159	- Forecasts are stored in MongoDB collection forecast_hourly.
160	
161	Better:
162	- Historical forecast issues must remain independently addressable by (location, valid_time, issue_time) because validation compares what was known at different issue times.
163	
164	## What makes a thing "load-bearing"
165	
166	- A decision or invariant whose violation would cause multiple parts of the system to become wrong, not merely require local refactoring.
167	- A thing is load-bearing when several of these are true: has high blast radius, crosses boundaries (i.e. services, persistence, APIs, ownership), other decisions depend on it, it protects an invariant,
168	is expensive to reverse, holds non-obvious rationale, long-standing.
169	
170	- Counter-test: if it can be changed locally without understanding the rest of the architecture, it is not load-bearing.
171	
172	## The loop
173	
174	Two rings, joined at /align.
175	
176	    session:   wake with /recall → /align → /conclude → (next session)
177	    delivery:  /ticket → /plan → /implement → /verify → /maintain → /ticket
178	
179	/align opens the delivery ring and is where it returns whenever a decision is needed:
180	/spec for load-bearing shapes, /plan when the governing docs contradict, /verify when a finding needs one, /maintain when maintenance surfaces one. /ticket⇄/plan and /implement⇄/verify iterate as pairs.
181	
182	Human checkpoints: every decision at /align; spec accepted; and, as their switches under
183	[Autonomy](#autonomy) set them, breakdown, commit, push and the next cycle at /maintain → /ticket.
184	
185	Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence.
186	
187	### Helpers
188	
189	- /impact determines the scope and load-bearingness of the shape. Use it to evaluate work volume and its ticketing shape (spec for load-bearing work, tickets for mechanical), work units slicing or whether a shape deserves further investigation due to hidden complexity.
190	- /discover to investigate hidden complexity, by detecting what else the shape is.
191	
192	## Self-improvement
193	
194	- A rule that was in place and did not fire was usually worded wrong. Register the failure in docs/rule-failures.md, or strike the entry it repeats, and propose the amendment that would have made it fire; /mechanism and /skill-up hold the means. Land the amendment in the same pass, showing its text first.
195	- A slip no rule covers is registered there too, described broadly enough to recognise its repeat;
196	  one proposes no rule.
197	- Keeping the register: an entry names the rules that were in play and proposes the amendment; a repeat strikes the entry it repeats rather than opening a second; an entry closes when its amendment lands, or is refused with its reason. Nothing here authorises deleting a rule.
198	
199	## Autonomy
200	
201	The project sets each switch in its local block, under *Project-local*; skills defer to those values.
202	A switch the project has not set is `ask`.
203	
204	| Switch | Meaning |
205	|---|---|
206	| commit | `ask`: commit only on explicit permission, per change. `auto`: commit when `/verify` has passed on the work. |
207	| push | `ask`: separate from commit, and /conclude's alone — no other reply asks, mentions or counts what waits on it. `never`, `auto`. |
208	| next-cycle | `ask`: starting the next ticket after one lands needs a nod. `auto`. |
209	| breakdown | `ask`: a /ticket split needs approval before minting. `auto`. |
210	| repair | `report`: a clear violation of an explicit rule inside authorized work is fixed and reported. `ask`: show it first. |
211	
212	`repair=report` holds only when all four are true: the governing rule is explicit, and cited; the
213	repair restores compliance inside the authorized work and keeps every other agreed contract; the
214	affected behaviour is understood well enough to say so; the result is verifiable against the
215	rule. Otherwise `/align`. *(the user, 2026-09-05)*
216	
217	## Project-local
218	
219	<installed by="mechanism-shape">
220	**R7** A project's own answers and overrides are authored in one file beside the entry file,
221	`local.rules.md`, in the rules-file format, and reach a file only as the local block — the
222	installed block whose owner is `local` — which the installer writes after every mechanism's block
223	there, so the project's answer is what a reader meets after core's rule. An override names the rule it
224	overrides. A local change to a rule is written in the local file, never into a skill or the entry
225	file, and re-installed. The local block is the project's,
226	not core's, and a redeploy preserves it.
227	</installed>
228	
229	## Straw dogs
230	
231	Wrap anything an open question's answer will change, as you write it — or, for text already
232	written, in the pass that opens the question: `<straw-dog question="q-N">`, bound to the question
233	whose answer will rewrite it, or in code a `TODO` naming `q-N` first. Treat *not yet*, *until*,
234	*once it exists*, *for now*, *untested* in your own text as the same signal: find the question, or
235	open one. Wrap at the authored home, never where the harness installs or derives it. Write the body
236	to stand on its own: it is what a recipient receives once the wrapper is stripped, so it names no
237	question or ticket — the binding does. Leave what no open question would change unwrapped.
238	
239	Follow a straw dog like any other rule until it is due, as the listing and the wake report; then
240	act on reality, rewrite it to what is now true, and do not treat the contradiction as a violation.

may name a path under `docs/` only when that path is a record a mechanism declares — the directory

A project's architecture, ADRs and glossary are the home for:
- Constitution — identity semantics, consistency model, source-of-truth rules
- Structure — service boundaries, data ownership, event/data flows, extension seams
- Load-bearing — see the definition below

A decision forms in the body of the question it answers and lands in one of these as it is made —
as a straw dog while an open question's answer can still change it. A decision about a
mechanism lands in that mechanism's doc, and what was refuted in its evidence.

Bad architectural documentation:
- Forecasts are stored in MongoDB collection forecast_hourly.

Better:
- Historical forecast issues must remain independently addressable by (location, valid_time, issue_time) because validation compares what was known at different issue times.

## What makes a thing "load-bearing"

- A decision or invariant whose violation would cause multiple parts of the system to become wrong, not merely require local refactoring.
- A thing is load-bearing when several of these are true: has high blast radius, crosses boundaries (i.e. services, persistence, APIs, ownership), other decisions depend on it, it protects an invariant,
is expensive to reverse, holds non-obvious rationale, long-standing.

- Counter-test: if it can be changed locally without understanding the rest of the architecture, it is not load-bearing.

## The loop

Two rings, joined at /align.

    session:   wake with /recall → /align → /conclude → (next session)
    delivery:  /ticket → /plan → /implement → /verify → /maintain → /ticket

/align opens the delivery ring and is where it returns whenever a decision is needed:
/spec for load-bearing shapes, /plan when the governing docs contradict, /verify when a finding needs one, /maintain when maintenance surfaces one. /ticket⇄/plan and /implement⇄/verify iterate as pairs.

Human checkpoints: every decision at /align; spec accepted; and, as their switches under
[Autonomy](#autonomy) set them, breakdown, commit, push and the next cycle at /maintain → /ticket.

Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence.

- /impact determines the scope and load-bearingness of the shape. Use it to evaluate work volume and its ticketing shape (spec for load-bearing work, tickets for mechanical), work units slicing or whether a shape deserves further investigation due to hidden complexity.

- A rule that was in place and did not fire was usually worded wrong. Register the failure in docs/rule-failures.md, or strike the entry it repeats, and propose the amendment that would have made it fire; /mechanism and /skill-up hold the means. The project sets each switch in its local block, under *Project-local*; skills defer to those values.
A switch the project has not set is `ask`.

|---|---|
| commit | `ask`: commit only on explicit permission, per change. `auto`: commit when `/verify` has passed on the work. |
| push | `ask`: separate from commit, and /conclude's alone — no other reply asks, mentions or counts what waits on it. `never`, `auto`. |
| next-cycle | `ask`: starting the next ticket after one lands needs a nod. `auto`. |
| breakdown | `ask`: a /ticket split needs approval before minting. `auto`. |
| repair | `report`: a clear violation of an explicit rule inside authorized work is fixed and reported. `ask`: show it first. |

`repair=report` holds only when all four are true: the governing rule is explicit, and cited; the
repair restores compliance inside the authorized work and keeps every other agreed contract; the
affected behaviour is understood well enough to say so; the result is verifiable against the
rule. Otherwise `/align`. *(the user, 2026-09-05)*

<installed by="mechanism-shape">

Wrap anything an open question's answer will change, as you write it — or, for text already
written, in the pass that opens the question: `<straw-dog question="q-N">`, bound to the question
whose answer will rewrite it, or in code a `TODO` naming `q-N` first. Treat *not yet*, *until*,

to stand on its own: it is what a recipient receives once the wrapper is stripped, so it names no
question or ticket — the binding does. Leave what no open question would change unwrapped.

act on reality, rewrite it to what is now true, and do not treat the contradiction as a violation.

# Meteoscape · DevOps setup

Records the operational/DevOps decisions for the project: toolchain, CI, deployment form, and
observability. The *architecture* contract lives in [`architecture.md`](./architecture.md); this
doc is the layer below it — how the project is built, checked, and run.

## Language & toolchain

- **Python 3.14+**, async throughout (`requires-python = ">=3.14"`).
- **[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** for packaging and environment management — it owns the
  Python toolchain, the virtualenv, and the lockfile (`uv.lock`). Chosen over pip/Poetry for its
  single-tool speed and reproducible locked syncs.
- Build backend: `uv_build`.

Quality tooling (pinned in `pyproject.toml`, dev group):

| Concern | Tool |
|---|---|
| Lint | `ruff check` |
| Format | `ruff format` (line length 100, double quotes) |
| Types | `pyright` |
| Tests | `pytest` + `pytest-asyncio` + `pytest-cov` |
| HTTP mocking | `respx` |
| Property tests | `hypothesis` |

## CI pipeline

GitHub Actions — [`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml). Triggers on push to
`main` and on every pull request; in-flight runs for the same ref are cancelled.

One `build` job on `ubuntu-latest`:

1. `uv sync --locked` — install the exact locked environment.
2. `uv run ruff check .` — lint.
3. `uv run ruff format --check .` — formatting gate.
4. `uv run pyright` — type check.
5. `uv run pytest` — tests.

Remote: `github.com/dveyarangi/meteoscape`.

> The pytest suite includes packaging and MCP-startup smoke coverage, unit and property tests, and
> mocked-provider integration coverage. Last-observed health and outstanding gate failures live in
> the [delivery status](./tickets/README.md); CI remains authoritative.

Live Provider parity checks (`uv run pytest tests/parity`) are deliberately **outside CI**:
`testpaths` scopes the default run to `tests/deterministic/`, keeping the gate network-free —
see the [Provider edge record](./edge/provider.md). Enforcement and routing of those checks are
[#41](./concerns.md#41-parity-evidence-is-unenforced-and-unrouted).

**Documentation integrity is gated.** The corpus is deliberately cross-referential — a claim lives
in one document and is cited from the rest — so two guard modules in the deterministic suite
(`test_docs_integrity_guard.py`, `test_docs_conventions_guard.py`) fail the ordinary pytest step
when that structure breaks: a live document's relative link or heading anchor stops resolving; any
tracked file carries a BOM, a stray control character, or a blocklisted invisible codepoint; a code
comment's doc pointer (a `#NN` concern ref, an `ADR-NNNN`, or a `.md` path in its canonical
repo-root form, `docs/edge/provider.md`) stops resolving; the delivery map and the ticket folders
disagree; or a session record's filename and H1 disagree about its number or date. Dated records —
`docs/sessions/`, `docs/tickets/done/`, `docs/rfc/done/`, `docs/dreams/` — are kept as written, so
their *outbound* links are exempt (a README inside such a directory stays gated); byte hygiene has

"""Shared corpus primitives for the documentation guards (docs/cicd.md § CI pipeline).

The two guard modules — integrity and conventions — walk the same repository universe and read
the same markdown grammar; those primitives live here so the guards stay stories about their own
rules. Everything takes explicit inputs, so synthetic corpora in `tmp_path` run through the exact
functions the live gates run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess
from collections import Counter
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

EXEMPT_PREFIXES = ("docs/sessions/", "docs/tickets/done/", "docs/rfc/done/", "docs/dreams/")
"""Dated-record directories: kept as written, so their outbound links are nobody's promise."""

_FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
_INLINE_CODE = re.compile(r"`[^`]*`")
_HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{1,6}\s+(.*)$")
_LINK = re.compile(r'!?\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\)')
_SLUG_DROPPED = re.compile(r"[^\w\- ]")


def universe(root: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Every file the gate speaks for: tracked plus untracked-but-unignored, exact case.

    Exact-case names from git catch case drift a Windows working tree hides from the Ubuntu CI
    checkout; including untracked files lets a freshly minted document resolve before `git add`.
    """
    listing = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files", "-z", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
        cwd=root,
        capture_output=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        check=True,
    )
    return [name for name in listing.stdout.split("\0") if name]


def strip_code(text: str) -> str:
    """The prose of a markdown document: fenced blocks and inline code removed.

    Links inside code are illustrations (`./RR-NNNN-slug.md` and friends), not citations.
    """
    prose: list[str] = []
    in_fence = False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if _FENCE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if not in_fence:
            prose.append(_INLINE_CODE.sub("", line))
    return "\n".join(prose)


def links(text: str) -> list[str]:
    """Inline link targets in the document's prose."""
    return _LINK.findall(strip_code(text))


def heading_anchors(text: str) -> set[str]:
    """GitHub-style anchor slugs for every heading outside fenced code."""
    anchors: set[str] = set()
    seen: Counter[str] = Counter()
    in_fence = False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if _FENCE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        heading = _HEADING.match(line)
        if heading is None:
            continue
        slug = _slugify(heading.group(1))
        repeat = seen[slug]
        seen[slug] += 1
        anchors.add(slug if repeat == 0 else f"{slug}-{repeat}")
    return anchors


def _slugify(heading: str) -> str:
    plain = re.sub(r"[*_`]", "", heading.strip().lower())
    return _SLUG_DROPPED.sub("", plain).replace(" ", "-")


def live(name: str) -> bool:
    """A maintained markdown document — one whose outbound links are a kept promise.

    A `README.md` inside a dated-record directory is maintained and counts as live.
    """
    if not name.endswith(".md"):
        return False
    if name.startswith(EXEMPT_PREFIXES):
        return name.rsplit("/", 1)[-1] == "README.md"
    return True


def resolve_name(source: str, relpath: str) -> str:
    """A relative link target as a repo-root name, `..`/`.` folded without touching the filesystem."""
    parts = source.split("/")[:-1]
    for segment in relpath.split("/"):
        if segment == "..":
            if parts:
                parts.pop()
        elif segment not in ("", "."):
            parts.append(segment)
    return "/".join(parts)

3	Work is tracked and argued in this repository. There is no external tracker: state, order and

9	## Naming

# Development process

Work is tracked and argued in this repository. There is no external tracker: state, order and
argument all live in these files, so nothing is registered anywhere else — no GitHub issues, no
issue numbers. What each document owns is [the documentation map](./README.md)'s; this page holds
what connects them — the naming that links the document family, and the skill loop that moves work
through it.

## Naming

The document family shares names, never content:

- A ticket names the work; its other artifacts take the same basename —
  `docs/tickets/01-0119-live-window-edge-tolerance.md` ↔ `docs/rfc/01-0119-live-window-edge-tolerance.md`.
  Each moves to its own `done/` on its own completion, basename intact; repositioning a ticket
  renames its RFC in the same change.
- Cite a ticket by its slug, never by number; cite a plan by its ticket's slug ("the TWC provider
  RFC"), never by a serial or position.
- A spec is a local markdown file under `docs/`, named for the effort — agree the filename with the
  user (the existing release contract is [`v1-requirements.md`](./v1-requirements.md); not every PRD
  is a requirements doc). A spec is argument rather than a work item, so it registers nothing; the
  tickets it decomposes into carry the work onto [the queue](./tickets/README.md).

The ticket's own scheme — `RR-NNNN-slug`, position allocation, subticket depth — is
[TICKET-FORMAT.md § Numbering](../.agents/skills/to-tickets/TICKET-FORMAT.md#numbering)'s, as is
the delivery-state vocabulary ([§ Status](../.agents/skills/to-tickets/TICKET-FORMAT.md#status))
and the mechanics of the `done/` move
([§ One basename per work item](../.agents/skills/to-tickets/TICKET-FORMAT.md#one-basename-per-work-item)).

## The loop

Each stage is a skill; each hands its artifact to the next. The whole is diagrammed in
[workflow.excalidraw](../.agents/skills/workflow.excalidraw).

- [/to-spec](../.agents/skills/to-spec/SKILL.md) argues a brief into a spec.
- [/to-tickets](../.agents/skills/to-tickets/SKILL.md) slices work into tickets and registers them
  in [the queue](./tickets/README.md) in the same pass.
- [/align](../.agents/skills/align/SKILL.md) settles a decision-bearing ticket's open questions;
  [/impact](../.agents/skills/impact/SKILL.md) traces a change's consequences before committing to
  it.
- [/plan-impl](../.agents/skills/plan-impl/SKILL.md) plans the ticket's RFC;
  [/implement](../.agents/skills/implement/SKILL.md) builds to it;
  [/review-impl](../.agents/skills/review-impl/SKILL.md) checks the build against its governing
  documents.
- [/commit](../.agents/skills/commit/SKILL.md) lands the change — never unasked.
- [/recall](../.agents/skills/recall/SKILL.md) reads where things stand;
  [/conclude](../.agents/skills/conclude/SKILL.md) records the session;
  [/sync-arch](../.agents/skills/sync-arch/SKILL.md) and
  [/edge](../.agents/skills/edge/SKILL.md) keep the architecture documents and edge records honest
  against the code.

---
name: commit
description: >-
  Use when committing or pushing changes to the repository.
---

Mechanism: not yet

- Commit the work in current session only. Do not commit changes of other session that might represent a work in progress. When in doubt, ask user.

- Look at pending changes; group them by content aligning with origin topic, ticket, rfc or change type (documentation, code, CI, skills).

- Separate implementation and documentation commits.

- Write the subject in the project's own convention, where it states one.

- In case the file changes belong to several groups, commit the file with the group forming its dominant topic and mention the bleed in that commit's message.

- Do not reference sessions in commit comments, sessions are ephemeral.

- Unless already working in branch or instructed to branch - commit to default branch.

- Work the person holds back stays on its own branch, never merged into the shared main until they
  release it: whatever stands on main may be published.

- When committing a code change, first run the checks the repository defines for itself — its
  linter, its formatter in check mode, its type checker, its tests. Pure doc changes need none
  of them. **Read them from where the project states them; never carry them here.** A commit
  skill holding a project's commands is a second home for them, and it is wrong for every
  project but the one it was written in.

- Commit and push only as the entry file's `commit` and `push` switches allow; a push is its own
  permission, never implied by a commit's.

Харнесс стоит в meteoscape. Он поставлен из remote (`github.com/dveyarangi/goodwolf-harness` на `fe0dbd3`); твой локальный клон установка не читала. Проверка целостности установленной копии после коммита проходит, CI проекта зелёный: ruff, format, pyright, 449 тестов.

Всё лежит на ветке `goodwolf-install`, в `main` не вливал и не пушил:

| 🪶 Commits | |
|---|---|
| `1d9ae8d` | SKILL: установка харнесса; старый корпус `.agents/` удалён целиком, как ты выбрал |
| `f478f3e` | CODE: ruff, pyright и проверка ссылок в документах больше не смотрят в `.agents/`; удалён тест старого `move_doc.py` |
| `d2bf1c6` | DOCS: раздел про цикл работы в `process.md` теперь ссылается на `AGENTS.md`; ссылки на формат тикетов ведут в новый скилл `ticket` |

Твои ответы записаны в `local.rules.md`: коммичу сам после зелёного `/verify`, push спрашиваю в `/conclude`, перед нарезкой на тикеты и перед следующим тикетом жду твоего «да». Проверки — CI плюс все проверки записей харнесса.

Из этого есть следствие: две проверки записей сейчас падают. Это проверки тикетов и edge-записей, а старые записи meteoscape ещё не в их формате. В edge-записях, например, указаны тесты, которых не существует. Пока это не исправлено, `/verify` никакую работу не пропустит. Значит, первая работа — перевести эти записи в формат харнесса.

Ещё три мелочи:
- `uv run` пытается пересобрать окружение и упирается в `meteoscape.exe`, который держит запущенный MCP-сервер. Проверки я гонял с `UV_NO_SYNC=1`. Когда остановишь сервер, один раз выполни `uv sync`.
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` с твоими правилами (правки через edit-инструменты, диаграммы, README) я не трогал. Он читается рядом с новым корневым `CLAUDE.md`.
- Правила харнесса действуют со следующей сессии: это её первая сессия, она начнётся с `/recall` и разбора проекта вместе с тобой.
